newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to cut 3,000 jobs in France - paper.
newsitem.headline: Renault to cut 3,000 jobs in France - paper.

text.p: French carmaker Renault is expected to announce plans to cut about 3,000 jobs in France on top of a plant closure in Belgium, the newspaper Les Echos said on Monday.
It said the plan would accelerate the pace of job cuts at the troubled company, which trimmed 1,641 jobs in 1996.
Restructuring charges associated with the Belgian plant closure and French job cuts should increase Renault's 1996 net loss to more than five billion francs ($875 million), the newspaper said.
Officials at Renault and its unions were not immediately available for comment.

Renault had warned the financial markets recently that it expected to show a significantly larger operating loss for 1996 than expected, leading most analysts to raise their operating loss forecast to over two billion francs.
The charge associated with the closure of Renault Industrie Belgique, which employs 3,100 people, has been reported by French newspapers at between 2.3 and 2.4 billion francs.
Despite an outcry in Belgium, chairman Louis Schweitzer said over the weekend that the company was sticking with its plan to close the plant and put the site up for sale.
The closure should result in annual savings of 850 million francs, Les Echos said.
At the end of 1995, Renault employed about 140,000 people.
The French newspaper La Tribune said Renault's Spanish subsidiary Fasa-Renault also swung into the red last year, losing 160 million francs.
